name: Bryon Hargis
profile: Aerospace engineer (Georgia Tech BSME, Johns Hopkins MS applied physics) who spent over a decade at Johns Hopkins APL and nearly six years at SpaceX, where he led national-security satellite sales and started Starshield. In November 2022 he co-founded Castelion with ex-SpaceX colleagues Sean Pitt and Andrew Kreitz to mass-produce low-cost hypersonic weapons. Castelion's Blackbeard missile is now a Navy program of record, and the company was valued at about $13B in late 2026.
interesting_fact: Castelion's Blackbeard hypersonic missile is designed to cost under $500,000 per unit; the company went from a $3M first Navy contract to over $500M in US government contracts.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days he lived on his own retirement savings and asked his co-founders up front at what point they would quit if they hadn't built anything. He describes his father's job at a nuclear power plant as 'like Homer Simpson'.
notes: Defense/hypersonics angle; has done long-form podcasts (The Generalist, Payload). Castelion's valuation has jumped well past Hurun's $3B figure. Press route: media@castelion.com.

name: Abhay Mitra
profile: IIT Delhi-trained engineer who led data-platform and other engineering teams at enterprise data-security company Rubrik before co-founding Nirvana Insurance in 2021 with Rushil Goel and Alex Carges. As CTO he builds the platform that uses connected-truck telematics for risk selection, usage-based pricing and safety monitoring. Nirvana raised a $100M Series D at a $1.5B valuation in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Nirvana was named the fastest-growing insurtech within its first year and has grown rapidly since selling its first policy in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first venture in his final year at IIT Delhi, and at Rubrik built several engineering teams from scratch and led the data platform team during its growth to $500M in revenue. He says IIT's computer science courses taught him 'the importance of first principles thinking'.
notes: Technical founder with a data-infrastructure background (Rubrik, Bidgely), a good fit for a data-center angle. Enjoys hiking and the beach (per CEO Insights India). Low media profile; route via press@nirvanatech.com.

name: Wang Qibin
current_role: Founder & CEO, PsiBot (灵初智能, Beijing/Shanghai)
profile: PhD and roughly 20-year product veteran in mobile phones, smart speakers and robotics (reportedly BlackBerry, Sonos China, Yunji and JD robotics) who founded PsiBot in September 2024. PsiBot builds reinforcement-learning-based vision-language-action models and dexterous hands for long-horizon manipulation in factories and warehouses. Bloomberg reported a round led by Chery at a $1.48B valuation in July 2026.
interesting_fact: PsiBot's Psi R1 model was demoed playing mahjong: the robot autonomously decides to pong, kong and declare a winning hand, slowly but much like a human player.
deep_cut_fact: He argues the best robot-training data comes from real workplaces, so PsiBot has workers wear exoskeleton data gloves while doing their normal jobs. He has said a robot makes economic sense once it costs less than about 24 months of local labour.
notes: Coverage is mostly Chinese-language (36Kr, Huxiu, TMTPost, Sina). The 24-month labour-cost rule comes from a June 2025 Sina interview cited by aiwiki.ai; I could not open the original.

name: Nick Hughes
current_role: Co-founder, M-KOPA (most recently listed as Chief Product Officer); Executive Fellow, London Business School Wheeler Institute
profile: British PhD scientist who, as Vodafone's head of social innovation, set up and ran M-Pesa, the Kenyan mobile-money service built with Safaricom. In 2010-11 he co-founded M-KOPA in Nairobi with Jesse Moore and Chad Larson, first selling pay-as-you-go solar home systems and now smartphones and digital credit to underserved customers in five African markets. He was awarded an OBE in 2017 for services to innovation in Africa.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited as the 'father of M-Pesa', which won him The Economist's innovation award in 2010; M-KOPA, which started with solar, reached 5 million customers and turned its first profit in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vodafone he worked at BP getting engineers to treat environmental problems as economic ones, work that fed into carbon-trading models. M-Pesa itself began as a micro-credit pilot seeded by a UK DFID Challenge Fund grant.
notes: Strong energy-access angle (pay-as-you-go solar, BP carbon-trading background). Leads LBS's Digital for Development initiative, so LBS is an alternative route. His current M-KOPA title is not confirmed for 2026; Jesse Moore is CEO and Rajeev Suri chairs the board.
